findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Employees were observed washing hands then using their newly-clean hands to turn off the faucet or dispense paper towels from the wall-mounted dispenser. CORRECTED- Inspector provided education. Employees need to use a paper towel or other barrier when dispensing paper towels and when turning off the faucet to prevent recontaminating their hands. Review handwashing procedures with all employees.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Raw shell eggs were eobserved stored on the top shelf of the short prep cooler, above squeeze-bottles of sauces and other ready-to-eat foods. Upon further discussion, PIC stated that the eggs are employee personal foods, not for service. CORRECTED- PIC designated the right-most door of the long prep cooler for storage of personal foods. The carton of eggs was moved to be stored away from foods for service. Ensure foods are stored to prevent potential cross contamination during storage.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Chlorine sanitizer in the 3 compartment sink was observed at 10ppm. CORRECTED- Inspector alerted the PIC, who added more chlorine to the sanitizer solution. Sanitizer was then observed at 50ppm Cl. Use test strips to verify sanitizer solution concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a concentration of 50-200ppm. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Six individual portions of mac & cheese were observed without dates in the 3 door cooler. CORRECTED- PIC labeled the portions with the date their original package was opened. Ensure all ready-to-eat TCS foods are labeled with the date they were opened, and used or discarded within 7 days after.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: Ambient thermometers were not observed in the 3 door cooler or in the long prep cooler. Provide ambient air thermometers for all cold holding units.
findings.citation_text: 4-203.12 Temperature Measuring Devices, Ambient Air and Water. (A) Ambient air and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled in Celsius or dually scaled in Celsius and Fahrenheit shall be designed to be easily readable and accurate to ±1.5°C in the intended range of use. (B) Ambient air and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±3°F in the intended range of use. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: The end of the shelving holding Cajun seasoning is unfinished and needs to be sealed. Paint or otherwise seal the bare end of the shelf.
findings.citation_text: 4-201.11 Equipment and Utensils. EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be designed and constructed to be durable and to retain their characteristic qualities under normal use conditions. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
1) Frost accumulation was observed on the interior of the right chest freezer. Defrost the freezer regularly to eliminate frost accumulation and maintain the interior of the freezer smooth and easily cleanable.
2) Price tag stickers were observed on metal lids in the prep coolers. Clean lids to remove stickers.
3) Food debris was observed on the interior of the microwave. CORRECTED- PIC discussed with an employee, who cleaned the inside of the microwave.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: The following physical facilities items are in need of attention: 
1) An electrical outlet on the cookline is askew and does not cover the area cut out of the wall. See that outlets fit properly on the walls. 
2) Seal the handsink to the wall. The handsink, while secured to the wall, is not firmly in place and has some give which may make sealing it to the wall difficult.
3) Cracked caulking is observed at the bathroom handsink. Recaulk to eliminate the cracks.
4) Ceiling tiles in bathroom are acoustic and should be vinyl coated - replace tiles

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: PIC is not a certified food protection manager. Ensure sufficient CFMs are on staff to cover all shifts of food prep and service.
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Facility does not have a written policy for clean up of vomit/diarrhea. CORRECTED- Inspector provided a vomit/diarrhea clean up policy. Keep available for review in case it is needed and ensure supplies are available.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Paper towels were not available at the kitchen handwashing sink. CORRECTED- PIC provided paper towels. Ensure paper towels are always available at all handwashing sinks.

[Pf]

If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Spray bottle that PIC presented as a sanitizer solution had no measurable Chlorine concentration. No bleach was available within the facility to make a fresh sanitizer solution. PIC had someone bring bleach to the facility so sanitizer could be made. Sanitizer observed  at 200 ppm. Facility cannot operate without sanitizer. Ensure it is available any time prepared food is available.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have a concentration of 50-200ppm. [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Blue spray bottle observed without any label. PIC stated that it contains sanitizer solution. CORRECTED- Bottle was labeled to indicate contents.
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Facility does not have a probe thermometer that is capable of registering cold temperatures. The probe thermometer that PIC presented is made to measure only hot temperatures. Ensure facility has a probe thermometer capable of registering both hot and cold temperatures.
4-302.12: (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. [Pf]

Facility does not have Cl (bleach) test strips to measure sanitizer concentration. Ensure test strips are available to monitor sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The following items are in disrepair and are in need of repair/replacement:
- Drywall around the back door (behind the meat chest freezer) is heavily damaged resulting in holes and areas which are not smooth, non-absorbent and/or easily cleanable. The drywall was must be sealed and holes filled to create smooth, easily cleanable surfaces.
- The back bathroom has a cracked/damaged flooring immediately past the entryway to the bathroom. Repair the floor so it’s smooth and easily cleanable.
- The floor, drywall, and base trim behind the toilet is damaged and molding. The toilet must be prevented from leaking and the water/molded area of tile/coving must be repaired/cleaned. 
- Caulking around the back of the triple sink is damaged and not smooth in several areas. Ensure that the triple sink is re-caulked so that the junction of the sink and the wall is smooth, non-absorbent and easily cleanable. 

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The mop in the back room was observed to be stored in the bottom portion of the mop bucket sitting in dirty water previously used to clean facility. Mops must be stored in the top portion of the mop bucket or hanging inverted against the wall to prevent contamination and facilitate air drying. Ensure that mops are stored properly, and that mop water is discarded promptly after use.

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
PIC (the only employee present) has not completed food handler training. Ensure any employees who work under a Certified Food Protection Manager have completed food handler training. See General Comments for additional explanation.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Inspector observed operator washing hands with improper procedure prior to serving nachos to consumers at the facility. Operator washed hands for less than 20 seconds. No barrier was used. When washing hands, ensure that hands are washed with soap for at least 20 seconds and that a barrier (such as a paper towel) is used to turn off the faucet. Operator was advised of proper procedure during previous routine inspection on 12/16/2022. This is a repeat violation from prior inspection. Procedure was corrected and operator is aware of the proper procedure to use when hand washing moving forward. Corrected on site. 

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
The hand washing sink in the prep area to the left of the triple sink was observed to be stocked with Old Spice body wash and not hand soap. Operator states that they have been using old spice body wash at the hand sink for the past three years. Operator was advised that hand soap must be used and that body wash is not appropriate for hand washing. Body wash is not formulated for hand washing and does not possess the same antimicrobial properties as hand soap. Hand soap was brought out to the hand sink during the inspection. Corrected on site. No additional follow up required.

6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed chemical sanitizer (bleach) used in the clear spray bottle at the back of the store has a concentration in excess of the capabilities of inspectors test strips to reach; test strips are effectively bleached out. Concentrations of chemical sanitizer must be between 100 and 200 ppm to be effective. Ensure that test strips are being used to confirm concentration and that concentrations between 100 and 200 ppm are achieved. Operator added water to the spray bottle bringing the concentration to 200 ppm Cl. Corrected on site. No additional follow-up required.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Individually packaged ice cream in the chest freezer at the north end of the store is observed to be in direct contact with ice. Ice cream packaging is not impervious to water penetration and may not be in contact with frozen condensation. Ensure that foods are protected from contamination by preventing accumulation of ice or other residue/debris from touching foods.

3-303.12: (A) PACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with ice or water if FOOD is subject to entry of water. (B) unPACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in contact with undrained ice. (C) Whole raw produce, cut, raw vegetables such as celery, carrots, potatoes, or tofu can be immersed in ice or water. (D) Raw poultry and raw FISH received in ice may remain in condition while in storage awaiting preparation, display, service, or sale.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Ice accumulated on the walls of both chest freezers in the service/display areas of the facility. The ice ranges in thickness from half an inch to two inches. Ice accumulation is significant enough to pose a contamination hazard to foods stored in the chest freezers. Ensure that the ice is removed from the chest freezers. 

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The mop in the back room was observed to be stored in the bottom portion of the mop bucket sitting in dirty water previously used to clean facility. Mops must be stored in the top portion of the mop bucket or hanging inverted against the wall to prevent contamination and facilitate air drying. Ensure that mops are stored properly.

6-501.113: Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.comment:
The following items are in disrepair and are in need of repair/replacement:

- There are three holes in the ceiling above the “True” display cooler which must be filled/sealed.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
The light in the bathroom is a miniature CFL type bulb and is observed to be uncovered and unshielded. The lightbulb is not shatterproof. Lightbulbs must be shielded, covered or shatterproof. Replace the light bulb in the bathroom with a shatterproof bulb or provide a cover.

6-202.11: Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated or otherwise shatter-resistant in certain areas.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 PIC washed hands without proper technique prior to preparing an order of nachos for a customer. Soap was not used, the process lasted less than 20 seconds, and the manual faucet was shut off prior to using paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed, and educational handout was provided for reference.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-102.11 (A), (B) & (C)(1), (4)-(16) Priority violations were observed during the inspection. See violations 11, 15, & 16 for details. A broken food thermometer was also available, which indicates heating temperature for cheese sauce and hot holding temperature for taco meat have not be monitored during daily operations. Person in charge (PIC) was advised on active managerial controls. A re-inspection will be conducted to verify a food thermometer is available and revisit active managerial controls.
Based on the risks inherent to the food operation, during inspections and upon request the PIC shall demonstrate to the regulatory authority knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the hazard analysis and critical control points, and the requirements of the Code.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
750.1110d - Restroom fixtures (toilet and sink) and the floor were soiled with buildup. The restroom also had an unpleasant odor. Clean the bathroom daily/as needed and empty the trash regularly.
 
Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Soap and paper towels were not present at the front counter handsink. The sink and upper ledge were soiled with general debris and hair trimmings (from shaving?? - mirror was present on back side of sink). Soap and paper towels were provided; maintain soap and paper towels at the handsink. Clean the front handsink, and maintain it clean.

A supply of soap and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each handsink. Handsinks and related fixtures must be maintained clean and in good repair.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text:
750.1170 - Front door was open upon arrival of inspector, and a proper fitting screen door was not present. Metal used to prop the door open was moved to close the door. The door did not self-close to be flush with the door frame, which resulted in a gap being present between the frame and the door. When the door was pulled shut gaps were observed along the top and bottom edges on the left side. 

Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects. Repair or replace the door so it is self-closing and tight fitting/vermin proof.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1300 - Spray bottle of unlabeled, clear liquid was observed under the 3 part sink by a bottle of ammonia. It was assumed to be ammonia based on smell, and inspector's test strip did not indicate a presence for free chlorine (test strips used prior to realizing the facility didn't have bleach - see #20a). Liquid was dumped down the sink during the inspection.

Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.citation_text:
750.1350 - Various unused items were observed in the storage area, including but not necessarily limited to, an old Good Humor freezer, a television, dish washer, pizza oven, hot plate, and cigarette display. Remove all unnecessary items from the facility.  

Only articles necessary for the operation and maintenance of the food service establishment shall be stored on the premises.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750-830g Provide a test kit suitable for testing your bleach sanitizing solution.  A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Approved source
findings.comment:
750-100 Observed the facility giving away homemade cookies. Cease this activity. Whether you are selling or generously giving the cookies away is not a factor. You may not have homemade cookies on the premises to give to the public. Save homemade cookies for personal enjoyment. 
Also, observed the facility operating as a Medium Risk facility. This was addressed during the last routine inspection. The facility is going to be upgraded to a Medium Risk establishment. The facility is hot holding and dipping cheese sauce for nachos. With the upgrade comes the need for a pre-opening inspection and a plumbing inspection. 
Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.  The use of home prepared or home canned foods is strictly prohibited.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment: 750-100 Two pound containers of ground beef were observed stored in the three door glass cooler. Packages were observed damaged with finger holes. The meat was observed white and sunk into a container filled with blood. The meat packages were also dated to sell by June 6, 2016. Items were discarded during the inspection. Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-130(b) Observed boxes of chips and candy being stored on the floor in the side room. Store foods at least 6" off the floor to allow for proper cleaning. Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 Observed the two reach-in freezers to be coated with frost accumulation. Defrost and clean the freezers. Also, observed the handles on the three door cooler to be broken. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750-830g REPEAT: Provide test strips for the bleach you will be purchasing to use as a sanitizing agent. Wet wiping cloths should be stored in the sanitizing solution between uses. Sanitizing bucket concentation should be 100ppm Cl. Bleach should also be used for sanitizing equipment that touches food. Your cheese sauce ladle and containers should be washed, rinsed, sanitized and dipped in a 50ppm Cl solution for 60 seconds.  A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
750-820d REPEAT: Facility does not have proper bleach or quatarnary ammonia on-hand for sanitizing. Provide bleach and educate staff on how to sanitize. 

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
750-880 Observed single-service containers stored on the floor in the extra storage room. Store containers up 6" off the floor. Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.
750-880 Observed take home containers stored food side up within the handsink. Move sindle-service items away from water source and invert the containers so the food contact side is protected from splash and possible cross contamination. Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Cross-connections, back-siphonage, back-flow prevented
findings.comment: 750-1080 Observed the hose at the triple sink to be hanging within the sink basin. Secure the hose sprayer so it doesn't hang into the basin.A hose shall not be attached to a faucet unless a backflow prevention device is installed and hangs above the fill line. Install backflow prevention device.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment: 750-1120(b) Observed the handsink to be obstructed by single-service takehome containers. Moved during the inspection. Cease storing items within the handsink. Keep the handsink free so hands are always able to be readily washed.  Lavatories shall be accessible to employees at all times.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment: 750-1120e Bathroom handsink is observed soiled and without a supply of paper toweling. Supply paper towels to this handsink and wash the sink. A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment: 750-1170 There is observed a gap beneath the front door. Seal the gap. Protect the frontdoor so that no daylight is visible around the frame.  Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Toxic items labeled and used properly
findings.comment: 750-1300 Observed an unlabeled spray bottle of cleaning solution. Labeled during the inspection. Label all chemical bottles with contents. Containers of poisonous or toxic materials necessary for the maintenance of the establishment shall be labeled in accordance with law. Properly label containers of toxic substances.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: 750-540 The facility is being upgraded to a Medium Risk establishment. Facility does not have a current FSSMC available. Provide a copy of certificate. All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

findings.title: Approved source
findings.comment: 750-100 Facility is currently permitted as a Retail operation and is serving hot held cheese sauce (with chips). Upgraded during inspection. Facility will be reclassified from a Retail to a Medium Risk Facility. See notes in the General Comments - you may NOT cool and reheat foods nor may you cook raw, thawed meat products. Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.  The use of home prepared or home canned foods is strictly prohibited.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.comment: 750-140(b)  Cooling was observed being conducted on the premises. This activity must cease. Cheese sauce was previously being cooked two cans at a time then cooled in the refrigerator overnight before being reheated to less than 165F. Cheese sauce should be hot held at 135F until it is completely used OR until the end of service when product should be discarded or saved for personal use. Any cooled foods saved from the facility must be marked 'Personal Use'. Cooked potentially hazardous foods shall be properly cooled from 140°F to 70°F within 2 hours and from 70°F to 41°F or below within 4 hours.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750-830g See violation #20. There are no bleach or quat test strips available in this facility. Provide bleach test strips for the kitchen. A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750-800b Facility does not have bleach available for sanitizing of cheese hot holding unit and serving utensils. Bleach was made available during the inspection. Staff was unaware of the sanitizing step necessary when washing dishes in a commercial kitchen. Discussed process: wash (detergent), rinse (clean water), and sanitize (bleach solution of 50-100ppm). MAKE SURE SANITIZING DISHES REST IN SINK FOR AT LEAST 60 SECONDS. To prevent cross-contamination, kitchenware and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use and following any interruption of operations during which time contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: 750-1060 The toilet room handsink faucets leak (both the hot and the cold). Repair faucet so leaks are eliminated.  All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment: 750-1120e Toilet room does not have paper toweling available for use.  A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment: 750-1170 Outside door was propped open upon the start of the inspection. Door was closed during inspection. Cease keeping door open to allow for the possible entrance of pests into the facility. Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
750-540 Facility needs to secure a full-time employee that is a certified food manager certificate holder. Manager on-site indicated that his uncle has such a certificate. Make this paperwork available to our office.  All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager.

POST INSPECTION NOTE: Pre-opening for the upgrade scheduled for next week. All related violations will be addressed during that inspection.
